title: FusedOp compatibility catalogue and oddball regressions
content:
Summary:
This note collects experiments, microbenchmarks, and compatibility observations for fused operator combinations across FlashAttention, paged-attention, and the fused MLP/residual/ln kernels. Goal: provide a concise compatibility catalogue + heuristics that the routing layer can consult before choosing a kernel variant for a request. This is intentionally an engineering-first lab notebook — lots of partial results and TODOs.

Why this matters:
- Fused ops can yield 1.2x–3x token throughput improvements but only under constrained inputs (seq_len, batch, head dims, dtype).
- Wrong fusion choice is causing rare correctness regressions (NaNs or off-by-one tokens) and subtle QoS regressions for streaming workloads.
- The runtime needs deterministic fallbacks and conservative heuristics to avoid customer-facing incidents.

Glossary and conventions used in the doc:
- flash = FlashAttention kernel family
- paged = our paged/KV-paged attention path (emits same API but different memory semantics)
- fused-mlp = combined linear-GELU-linear pattern fused in a single kernel
- fused-ln-res = fused layernorm + residual add kernel used in last-resid accumulation
- dtype: fp16 = half, bf16 = bfloat16, fp32 = single
- seq/batch/headdim = sequence length, batch size, hidden/head dim respectively

Experiment methodology (short):
- Host: c5g.2x (dev GPU host for CI) and prod GPU node a100-80gb for target numbers.
- Repeat each microbenchmark 10 times, discard top/bottom 1, report median.
- Instrumentation: nvprof-equivalent sampling traces and the in-runtime kernel timestamp hooks. Also collect GPU utilization, SM occupancy, and L2 bandwidth counters (where accessible).
- Correctness: regression harness runs model forward for deterministic input streams and compares outputs to CPU reference (fp32) with tolerance 1e-3 L2 norm and token-level equality for logits where applicable.

Top-level findings (short):
1) Fusion compatibility is a 3D decision space: (shape, dtype, cache/streaming). Many heuristics can be simple thresholds, but there are ~7 notable edge cases that force fallback.
2) FlashAttention + fused-mlp shows speedups for seq >= 512, head_dim <= 128, batch <= 8; but when kv-paging is enabled, flash occasionally has extra copy overheads that make paged+non-fused path faster.
3) Fused-ln-res sometimes changes numerical rounding order causing token-level divergence on long-lived KV caches (>1024 tokens) for bf16; we recommend fp16-only fused-ln-res in production for now.
4) Streaming (prefix cache reuse) is the most fragile scenario: kernel choices that assume contiguous KV buffers break when prefix eviction/paged fills happen.

Compatibility matrix (selected rows) — ASCII table of common combos we tested

Model-shape | Dtype | KV-mode | Fused-attn | Fused-mlp | Observed perf delta vs baseline | Correctness notes
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
gpt2-like  B=1 S=256 H=64  fp16    in-memory   flash       yes        +1.6x                         OK
gpt2-like  B=1 S=1024 H=64 fp16    paged       flash       yes        +1.9x                         OK
gpt2-like  B=4 S=2048 H=128 bf16    paged       flash       yes        +1.1x                         NaNs observed after ~1500 tokens
bert-large B=2 S=512 H=64  fp16    in-memory   fallback    no         -0.9x                        OK
opt-6b    B=1 S=4096 H=128 bf16    paged       flash       no         +0.3x                        token-shift in logits

Notes on the table:
- Observed perf delta measured vs non-fused baseline implemented in the runtime (sequential kernels). Values are median of runs on A100-80GB.
- The 'fallback' path is usually paged + unfused ops. Negative perf delta indicates fused attempt slower than default (common when fusion adds copy/prefetch overhead).

Notable regressions and root-cause hypotheses (detailed):
1) NaNs in bf16 + fused-mlp + flash (paged)
   - Repro steps: run bench_kernels.py --model opt-1.3b --seq 2048 --batch 4 --dtype bf16 --kv paged --enable-fusion mlp,attn --kernel flash
   - Symptom: NaN appears in block 47 of layer 18 only when sequence exceed ~1500 tokens. CPU reference OK.
   - Investigation: trace shows an intermediate gemm accumulation overflowing and then reduced precision in bf16. The fused-mlp kernel uses an accumulator with fp16 accumulation in one code path. When paired with flash's fused attention prefetch, memory alignment triggers a different reduction order.
   - Mitigation: force fp32 accumulation for bf16 inputs in fused-mlp path (costs ~5–8%).

2) Token-shift (off-by-one logits) with paged-attn + fused-ln-res on long prefixes
   - Repro steps: incremental stream where prefix is paged out & then re-filled while streaming new tokens.
   - Symptom: logits move by a constant offset starting after refill; model still converges but top-1 token differs intermittently.
   - Investigation: subtle ordering difference: fused-ln-res applies residual add before a tiny in-place reorder used by paged refill logic. The paged refill expects the non-fused ordering.
   - Mitigation: add an ordering fence when paged mode is active or prefer non-fused-ln-res for paged flows.

3) Slowdown for small batch high-headdim combos when flash+fused-mlp enabled
   - Root cause: fusion introduces intermediate transpose + aligned buffers that hurt tensor core occupancy when head_dim not divisible by 32. The baseline had a tiled fallback that matched occupancy better.
   - Heuristic: only enable fused-mlp when head_dim % 32 == 0 OR head_dim <= 128 with batch >= 2.

Microbench commands and example outputs (copy-paste runnable in CI lab):
- bench_kernels.py --model gpt2 --seq 512 --batch 1 --dtype fp16 --kernel flash --fuse attn,mlp --repeats 10
  -> median tokens/sec 18750 (baseline 11000), wall clock 0.9s per batch
- bench_kernels.py --model gpt2 --seq 4096 --batch 1 --dtype bf16 --kv paged --kernel flash --fuse attn
  -> median tokens/sec 4100 (baseline 3900), but checksum mismatch after 30 mins of streaming
- microprof --trace kernels --prefix bench/gpt2-seq512-flash.json
  -> generates timeline used to attribute ~14% time to memcpy prefetch in fused path (only when paged enabled)

Instrumentation tips for triage:
- Always capture both in-runtime timestamps and nvprof/Nsight for the failing run; ordering issues are easy to miss with only CPU timers.
- Capture sequence length distribution and cache fill/evict trace. Add a triage flag to reproduce the exact page eviction schedule.
- Add a minimal reproducible test that toggles only one heuristic at a time (e.g., only disable fused-ln-res).

Routing heuristics proposal (conservative defaults for runtime):
1) If kv-mode == paged and streaming==true => prefer non-fused-ln-res and non-fused-attn for seq < 2048; allow flash-attn with fused-mlp only if (dtype==fp16 && head_dim%32==0).
2) If dtype==bf16 and total_tokens_seen > 1024 => avoid fused-mlp unless fp32-accum enabled.
3) For small batches (batch==1) & head_dim not divisible by 32 => disable fused-mlp.
4) Always run a short validation pass on the first 128 tokens (cheap checksum) after switching kernel variants in live traffic; revert on mismatch.

Regression test suite additions (CI):
- Add long-prefix streaming test for bf16 with paged mode (run ~2k tokens) to the nightly long tests. Label as slow but required for fusion safety.
- Add randomized eviction schedule generator used in local repro to stress ordering fences.
- Add synthetic worst-case microbench harness that tries head_dim in {64,96,128,160,192,256} and records perf & correctness for each fused combination.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Investigate whether changing accumulation precision in fused-mlp to fp32 for bf16 inputs could be tuned dynamically (only where needed) to reduce perf hit.
- Evaluate if a small hardware-assisted checksum (CRC) on KV pages could detect silent token-shifts earlier with negligible overhead.
- Explore compiler-time fusion (outside runtime) for certain model archetypes that can guarantee deterministic ordering.

Action items (short):
- [Asha] Create CI job for bf16-paged streaming (RDINF-5421) — due 2024-11-10.
- [Miguel] Prototype fp32-accum flag in fused-mlp and run perf sweep across head_dim values — due 2024-11-01.
- [Elliot] Add validation pass (first-128-token checksum) to kernel switcher and test on staging traffic — due 2024-11-05.

Appendix: quick decision table for routing layer (to implement as code):
- if paged:
    if streaming: prefer fallback unless (dtype==fp16 && head_dim%32==0 && seq>=512)
    if non-streaming: allow flash-attn fused if seq>=1024 and batch<=8
- if in-memory:
    prefer fused ops for seq>=256 when head_dim%32==0
    else use baseline unfused for safety

End of note. This is a working doc — add experiments and test results here as they come in.
